notes: Date: 1 January 1291. The War of the Sicilian Vespers continues: Sicily (with Malta and Djerba) under James II of Aragon, Naples and Provence under Charles II of Anjou.

The Latin East: only Acre, Tyre, Sidon, Beirut, Haifa, Atlit and the Templar Tortosa remain; all fall between May and August 1291. They are modelled as the Kingdom of Jerusalem of Henry II of Cyprus; the military orders (Hospitallers, Templars, Teutonic Knights) hold quarters and castles in it.

Northern Italian signori: Visconti (Milan), della Scala (Verona), Este (Ferrara, Modena since 1288, Reggio since 1289), Bonacolsi (Mantua), da Camino (Treviso). Many smaller communes (Pavia, Piacenza, Parma, Cremona, Brescia, Bergamo, Como, Asti, Alessandria, Pistoia, Volterra) are not modelled as realms yet: a gap.
Meinhard II of Gorizia-Tyrol holds Tyrol, the duchy of Carinthia (1286) and Carniola in pledge (from 1282); modelled as one realm.
Sardinia: Arborea (judges of Bas-Serra), Pisan Cagliari and Gallura (Nino Visconti expelled 1288), the Genoese Doria and Sassari in the old Logudoro.
Hungary: the great oligarchs (Kőszegi, Csák, Aba, Šubić, Borsa) are not modelled separately.
Thessaly (Great Vlachia) of the sons of John I Doukas and the Byzantine Durazzo (1288-96) differ from 1356.

states.dynasty_note: Pope Nicholas IV (Girolamo Masci, the first Franciscan pope), 1288-92. Romagna is under papal rectors since 1278; the Comtat Venaissin papal since 1274.

summary.en: Nicholas IV preaches a new crusade for Acre and backs the Angevins against Aragonese Sicily.
summary.de: Nikolaus IV. predigt einen Kreuzzug für Akkon und stützt die Anjou gegen das aragonesische Sizilien.

coa.blazon: Gules, two keys in saltire Or and argent beneath a papal tiara

states.dynasty_note: House of Anjou. King of Sicily without the island; also Count of Provence and Forcalquier, overlord of Achaea, and lord of Corfu and the Albanian coast at Kanina and Butrint.

coa.blazon: Azure semé-de-lis Or, a label gules

states.dynasty_note: House of Barcelona: James, second son of Peter III, King of Sicily since 1285; heir of Aragon (from June 1291). Roger of Lauria holds Djerba and the Kerkennah islands (1284).

coa.blazon: Per saltire Or paly gules and argent an eagle sable

states.dynasty_note: Judicate of Arborea.
Doge since November 1289. Crete, Modon and Coron are Venetian colonies; Negroponte is ruled by Lombard triarchs under a Venetian bailo; Ragusa has a Venetian count.

coa.blazon: Azure, a winged lion passant Or holding a book

ruler.name: Captains of the People (Oberto Spinola, Corrado Doria)

states.dynasty_note: Commune under two Ghibelline captains of the people. Victor over Pisa at Meloria (1284). Pera (Galata) since 1267; Caffa is modelled as its own city. The Doria hold Alghero and Castelgenovese in Sardinia; Sassari is a commune in the Genoese orbit.
Ghibelline commune, captain of war Guido da Montefeltro (1289-93); holds Cagliari and Gallura in Sardinia.
Guelph commune; victor at Campaldino (11 June 1289).
Guelph commune under the government of the Nine (from 1287).

coa.blazon: Per fess argent and sable (the Balzana)

states.dynasty_note: Guelph commune.
Ghibelline commune, defeated at Campaldino.
Guelph commune within the Papal States.

coa.blazon: Argent, a griffin rampant gules crowned Or

states.dynasty_note: Montefeltro lordship.

coa.blazon: Bendy Or and azure, a chief Or with an eagle sable
Azure, three towers argent on three peaks vert

states.dynasty_note: Guelph commune (the Pepoli lordship comes only in 1337).

ruler.name: Ottone Visconti, archbishop; Matteo Visconti, captain of the people

states.dynasty_note: Archbishop Ottone Visconti rules Milan since 1277; his great-nephew Matteo is captain of the people (1287) and becomes imperial vicar in 1294.

coa.blazon: Argent, a serpent azure crowned Or devouring a child gules

states.dynasty_note: Scaliger lordship (since 1277).

coa.blazon: Gules, a ladder argent ensigned with an imperial eagle sable

states.dynasty_note: Bonacolsi lordship; Pinamonte is deposed by his son Bardellone later in 1291.

coa.blazon: Barry of six Or and sable

states.dynasty_note: Este lordship; Modena (1288) and Reggio (1289) accepted Obizzo as lord.

coa.blazon: Azure, an eagle argent crowned Or

states.dynasty_note: Free commune ruling Vicenza (the Carrara lordship begins only in 1318).
The da Camino lordship of Treviso, Feltre and Belluno (1283-1312).
Patriarch of Aquileia (1273-99), lord of Friuli.
Albert II, brother of Meinhard II, holds Gorizia, the Puster valley and Istrian lordships (division of 1271).
Meinhard II, Count of Tyrol, Duke of Carinthia since 1286, holds Carniola and the Windic March in pledge from the Habsburgs; father-in-law of Albert of Austria. Controls the bishopric of Trent.

coa.blazon: Argent, an eagle gules crowned or

states.dynasty_note: William VII, the Great Marquis, has been held in an iron cage by the Alessandrians since September 1290 (dies February 1292); his son John I acts.
Count since 1285; Turin and Pinerolo are held by his nephew Philip of Savoy under him (the principality of Piedmont/Achaea dates from 1294-1301). Bresse through his marriage to Sibylle of Baugé.

The last Árpád, crowned 23 July 1290 after Ladislaus IV was murdered. Charles II of Naples claims the crown for his son Charles Martel; the great lords (Kőszegi, Csák, Aba, Šubić) act almost on their own.

coa.blazon: Per pale: barry gules and argent; azure semé-de-lis Or

states.dynasty_note: The former Serbian king Dragutin rules Mačva, Belgrade (1284), Usora and Soli as a vassal of Hungary.
Banate of Bosnia under Hungarian overlordship; Usora and Soli belong to Dragutin.

coa.blazon: Azure, a bend argent between fleurs-de-lis Or

states.dynasty_note: King since 1282; took Skopje (1282) and northern Macedonia from Byzantium. Zeta and Hum belong to the realm.
Commune under a Venetian count.
Tsar since 1280, tributary to Nogai of the Golden Horde (his son Theodore Svetoslav is a hostage there); he flees to Byzantium in 1292.

coa.blazon: Gules, a lion rampant Or crowned

states.dynasty_note: Despot Shishman, a Cuman-Bulgarian lord, vassal of Nogai.
Andronikos II (1282-1328). The Anatolian frontier is crumbling under the Turkmen; Durazzo was recovered from the Angevins in 1288; the Zaccaria hold Phocaea under the emperor.

coa.blazon: Gules, a cross Or between four betas Or

states.dynasty_note: Despotate of Epirus; allied with the Angevins against Byzantium.
The sons of the sebastokrator John I Doukas (d. c.1289), Constantine and Theodore, under their mother Hypomone.
Princess since 1289 with her husband Florent, vassals of Charles II of Naples.
Duke since 1287 under the regency of his mother Helena Angelina Komnene; Argos and Nauplia, Salona and Bodonitsa are fiefs of the duchy.

coa.blazon: Per saltire Or paly gules and argent with eagles sable (Aragon-Sicily)

states.dynasty_note: Duchy of the Archipelago (Naxos) under Venetian protection.

Henry II of Cyprus, crowned King of Jerusalem at Tyre in 1286. The Hospitallers, Templars and Teutonic Knights hold quarters and castles (Atlit, Tortosa, Sidon's sea castle). Acre falls on 18 May 1291, the rest by August.

summary.en: The last crusader coast. Sultan al-Ashraf Khalil is gathering the army that will besiege Acre in April.
summary.de: Die letzte Kreuzfahrerküste. Sultan al-Aschraf Chalil sammelt das Heer, das im April Akkon belagern wird.

states.dynasty_note: House of Lusignan.
Armenian Kingdom of Cilicia, vassal of the Ilkhan.

coa.blazon: Or, a lion rampant Gules crowned

name.en: Siege of Acre and the end of the crusader states
name.de: Belagerung von Akkon und das Ende der Kreuzfahrerstaaten
